_what_this_is: The DCP pipeline's contract. Every stage listed here MUST have a scheduled job, and every unbuilt item MUST stay visible. tests/test_the_pipeline_cannot_lose_a_stage.py enforces both at the pre-push pytest gate.
_why_it_exists: PR #506 migrated CI from GitHub Actions to Railway and silently DELETED the extract-to-review stage. Nothing failed, nothing alerted; the pipeline just stopped half-way and stayed that way for months. docs/DCP_PIPELINE_ARCHITECTURE_2026-06.md calls the fix 'the single check that would have caught #506; build it first'. It was specified on 2026-06-20 in commit 4115dbe6, whose own message says 'enforced by gates, not documentation' and ends 'Docs-only.' — 32 lines of markdown and no code. This file is that check finally existing.
_source: docs/DCP_PIPELINE_ARCHITECTURE_2026-06.md §4 Phase 0/1, §5.2 operating model, §5.3 enforced testing

stages.purpose: Detect: fetch each council source, compare bytes, set needs_extraction + content_hash.
stages.if_deleted: No chapter is ever flagged as changed again. Councils amend their DCPs and nothing notices — the served text silently goes stale with no error anywhere.

stages.purpose: Extract-to-review: re-read flagged chapters in memory and enqueue the diff. NO provision writes.
stages.if_deleted: THIS IS THE STAGE #506 DELETED. Detection keeps flagging chapters and nothing ever reads them, so the queue stays empty and the pipeline looks healthy while doing nothing.

stages.purpose: Quarterly full re-read of every active chapter, independent of the byte signal.
stages.if_deleted: A silent in-place amendment that does not move the byte hash is never found. This stage exists because the byte signal both false-positives on re-exports and false-negatives on in-place edits.

stages.purpose: Commit chapters whose queue rows a human approved, currency-guarded.
stages.if_deleted: Approved work never reaches regulatory_provisions. A reviewer clears the queue and nothing changes for users.

stages.purpose: Rule formulation: turn committed provision TEXT into structured queryable rules (v2_extracted_rules, v2_extraction_status). Fill-blanks-only, so it is idempotent.
stages.if_deleted: Provisions are served as PROSE with no structured rule behind them. Measured 2026-09-22 before this stage was scheduled: 11,389 of 19,243 served actionable provisions (59%) had no verdict at all, because this pipeline existed, worked, and was never run. The numbers a planner reads then come from hand-run per-council scripts instead, which is why they went stale.

stages.purpose: Alert on chapters whose PDF changed but which have not been re-read.
stages.if_deleted: A chapter wedged between detect and extract raises no alarm — the failure mode the dead-man's-switch exists for.

stages.purpose: Detect amendments to SEPPs/LEPs in instrument_registry.
stages.if_deleted: Served state law silently cites superseded provisions.

guards.doc: §5.2 invariant 8 — external dead-man's-switch per stage, + §7 'keep healthchecks.io as the independent external watchdog'. Rule 4 of ce-dcp-unattended-pipeline-PROMPT-2026-09-22: 'silence is an alarm'.
guards.purpose: Every stage refuses to look healthy while it has no working dead-man's switch. A missing HC_PING_URL, a placeholder, another stage's check, or a ping that does not land each alert by name and exit EXIT_NO_DEADMAN_SWITCH — and a misconfigured URL is deliberately NOT pinged, because pinging another stage's check holds that stage's alarm green.
guards.if_deleted: ping_healthcheck goes back to `if not url: return`, and a stage with no switch is indistinguishable from a watched one. Measured 2026-09-28 on the live Railway fleet in exactly that state: six services shared the literal value https://hc-ping.com/placeholder-satellite and four more carried nothing at all, so nothing anywhere alerted on silence. That is how the DCP source sweep stopped for 12 days with every dashboard green and DQ-70 reading fixed.
guards.residual: This guard makes the CLIENT side loud. It cannot create the healthchecks.io checks, cannot set one URL per Railway service, and cannot tell that two services share one OPAQUE UUID ping URL — only a slug one. Those are operator actions plus a fleet-wide config check, and this entry does not claim them.

_guards_rule: A guard listed here must keep existing, keep being defined in the file named, and keep the test named. `guards_floor` may only RISE — the mirror of unbuilt_ceiling, which may only FALL. Deleting a guard to make a change pass is the failure mode: #506 deleted a whole stage and nothing noticed.

unbuilt.what: Claim queue rows with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so concurrent workers cannot double-process.
unbuilt.verified_absent_on: 2026-09-22, grep for 'FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED' across scripts/ services/ tests/

unbuilt.what: A poison item escalates to a human instead of being retried forever or dropped.
Real council PDF fixtures + expected provision output, asserted offline, so a pdfplumber bump or page-range edit that changes output blocks the push.
Byte-identical-number changes commit themselves; 5% sampled and logged. The human gate stays on cited numbers and clause changes ONLY.
unbuilt.why_it_matters: Its absence is the reason the queue holds thousands of rows rather than 'only real, risky changes' as §5.2 requires — and why a backlog of 8,875 was bulk-approved in one night on 2026-09-09, pushing 578 bad rows live.
unbuilt.verified_absent_on: 2026-09-22, no cosmetic lane in the commit path

unbuilt.what: Per-control type/unit/range validation (clause format, units present, setback < ~30m). Failure routes to a human, never a live write.

_ceiling_rule: unbuilt_ceiling may only FALL. Raising it to accommodate a new gap is how a ratchet stops meaning anything — the same rule DQ-33's floor carries. Build the item, then lower the number.
